💡 Hierarchical LATP particles (5–500 nm) build a hybrid solid–liquid Li⁺ network in thick cathodes (27 mg cm⁻²). Nanograins lower desolvation energy and stabilize CEI; submicron particles bridge pores, raising diffusion and transference. This enables 102 vs 36 mAh g⁻¹ at 0.75C and −10 °C, advancing fast-charging high-energy batteries.

💡 The novelty lies in a multifunctional separator (PTT-GF-D) combining ordered nanoporous channels with a highly negatively charged surface, using electric field–pore size synergy to regulate liquid-phase mass transport. Advanced Energy Materials | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 Operando XRF tracking reveals that Mn²⁺ electrolyte additives improve cycling by supplying extra redox-active Mn during charge, not merely by suppressing cathode dissolution. This underscores the need to directly track Mn²⁺ and address both dissolution and redeposition to improve reversibility.
🏷 aqueous zinc battery · MnO2 cathode · Mn additive · operando XRF · dissolution-redeposition

Advanced Science | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 The novelty lies in co-designing a hybrid organic-aqueous electrolyte with thin polypropylene separators, overcoming the hydrophobicity that makes Li-ion separators incompatible with aqueous Zn-ion batteries. This enables uniform Zn plating, suppresses hydrogen evolution, and extends cycling to 4360 h. Replacing thick glass fiber separators boosts pouch cell energy density over 2.5-fold, offering a practical route to high-performance Zn-ion batteries.
